 Dated this the 5th day of March, 2025
 Judgment

The writ petition is preferred by the legal heirs of the owner of the property having an extent of 1 Acre 38.5 cents of property comprised in Survey Nos.1048/1, 1048/2, 1048/4 of Ernakulam Village by virtue of Partition Deed No. 608/1955 of Thrippunithura SRO.
2.

The writ petitioners have preferred this petition for completing the acquisition proceedings and for awarding the compensation for the property acquired by the 3 rd respondent for the purpose of widening the road, as per the present market value.

The authorities of the 2nd respondent informed the petitioners' mother that they would like to construct a road through the southern boundary of the said property and acquisition proceedings will be initiated soon and sanction was accorded to construct a wall leaving the property having an extent of 20 cents which is having a width of 36 links.
On getting permission, the petitioners' mother constructed a wall leaving 20 cents of property having an extent of a width of 2025:KER:18575 36 links.
However, even without initiating any acquisition proceedings, the property was taken over by the Corporation.
3. Now, it is the case of the petitioners that the 20 cents of property sought to be acquired is still being used by the Corporation as a road without adopting proper procedures.
However, no compensation has been paid for the land.

4. In response to that the learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent submitted that the writ petition is not maintainable because they approached the court after 20 years and Ext.P9 notice was issued already for completing the procedure.
However, that was not accepted and acted accordingly.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that although the notice was received, the Corporation has not taken any effective steps.
Even stamp papers were not purchased to that effect to complete the proceedings.
The property is still in the custody of the petitioners though it is being used as a road.

The petitioners are ready to complete the procedure either through a negotiable purchase scheme or by receiving compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short ' the Act,
2013').

sentences.text: Considered the contentions advanced across the Bar.
Going by the pleadings, it appears that the property was taken into custody by the Corporation in the year 1990 itself and it is being utilised as road.
However the further formalities, with respect to change of ownership and the nature of the land, have not been done by the Corporation, except issuing Ext.P9 notice.

8. In support of the contention, learned counsel for the petitioners brought my attention to the reported decision in 2020 (1) KLT 430 (SC) in Vidya Devi v. State of Himachal Pradesh in which the Apex Court held that:
"the right to property ceased to be a fundamental right by the Constitution (Forty Fourth Amendment ) Act, 1978, however, it continued to be a human right in a welfare State, and a Constitutional right under Article 300 A of the Constitution.
Article 300 A provides that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

entities.text: Vidya Devi v. State of Himachal Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The State cannot dispossess a citizen of his property except in accordance with the procedure established by law.

The obligation to pay compensation, though not expressly included in Article 300 A, can be inferred in that Article."
2025:KER:18575 9.
Under such circumstances, the 3 rd respondent has to take necessary steps to grant compensation to the petitioners either through negotiable purchase scheme or by taking steps under the Act, 2013.
10. If they are preferring for a negotiable purchase, the process shall be completed within one month.
Otherwise, for adopting procedure under the Act, 2013, the entire proceedings shall be completed within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this Judgment.
The writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
